title: Low Tide Radio
label: Undertow Records
review: A record that trusts silence as much as sound. The production keeps everything a few feet underwater — vocals blurred at the edges, guitars that arrive like weather rather than notes. It drags a little in the back third, but the best songs here are the kind you want to replay the second they end.

title: Concrete Season
label: Self-released
review: Front-loaded with the album's three best ideas, then coasts. Iyer's falsetto is the real instrument here, and when the arrangements get out of its way — as on the title track — the record is genuinely special. Elsewhere it leans on the same drum pattern a little too often.

title: Everyone I Know Is Tired
label: Gray Matter
review: Tight, furious, and eleven minutes shorter than it needs to justify how good it is. Every song has a hook buried inside the noise, and the rhythm section sounds like it's trying to get somewhere the guitars aren't allowed to go. Easily the tightest thing this band has made.
